title: Composite Functions from Graphs
explanation: LESSON OBJECTIVE
Evaluate composite functions directly from two graphs, respecting each graph’s input domain. The inside function is evaluated first.
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
A graph is a collection of input-output pairs. To read f(2), find x=2 on the horizontal axis, move to the f curve, then read its y-value.
KEY DEFINITIONS
Function: a rule giving one output for each permitted input. Domain: allowed inputs. Composition f(g(x)): first evaluate g(x), then use that result as an input to f.
CORE RULE
For f(g(a)), start INSIDE: a → g(a) → f(g(a)). The output of g must belong to the domain of f. Reverse order usually changes the result.
READ THE GRAPH
Use the colored graph legends and the marked solid endpoints. An endpoint is included in the domain; no curve beyond the endpoint means the function is undefined there.
HOW IT WORKS
1. Locate the original x on the inner graph. 2. Read its y. 3. Use that y as an x on the outer graph. 4. Read the outer y. 5. Check both domains.
WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — BASIC
On Graph A, g(0)=2. Then f(2)=3. Therefore f(g(0))=3. Follow the two arrows in that order.
WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — ORDER MATTERS
On Graph A, f(1)=1, then g(1)=3. So g(f(1))=3. This happens to match f(g(0)), but the inputs and operations are different.
WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — UNDEFINED
On Graph A, f(−2)=−5. The g curve only accepts x from −3 through 3. Therefore g(f(−2))=g(−5) is undefined.
WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — NONLINEAR GRAPH
On Graph B, q(2)=−1. Read p(−1)=−3 from the parabola. Hence p(q(2))=−3.
WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — SOLVE BACKWARD
On Graph A, f(g(x))=7 means f(t)=7, so t=4 on the f graph. Then g(x)=4, which occurs at x=2. Both inputs are in range.
VISUAL GRAPH BLOCK

Graph A uses straight segments, Graph B includes a parabola, and Graph C includes a V-shaped absolute-value graph. All plotted coordinates are calculated from the function rules and restricted domains.
COMMON MISTAKES
Reading the outer function first; treating f(g(x)) as multiplication; using an output outside the outer function’s domain; extending a curve beyond its solid endpoint.
EXAM STRATEGY
Write a two-step chain: inner value → outer value. For a multiple-choice question, eliminate any option that ignores a domain restriction. Use the graph only where it is defined.
QUICK CHECK
On Graph C, k(2)=1 and h(1)=0, so h(k(2))=0. Try k(h(2)) independently: h(2)=1, k(1)=2. The order changes the answer.
LESSON RECAP & NEXT STEP
Inside first, outside second; verify the inner output is allowed as an outer input. Now complete Practice, review 18 worked solutions, and submit the five-question Lesson Test.

video_en: Welcome
Composite functions from graphs. Today you will read two function graphs in sequence, and check their domains.
The central idea
The expression f of g of x means apply g first. Take the output of g and use it as the input of f.
Graph A
Look at f of x equals two x minus one and g of x equals x plus two. Each line has marked endpoints.
First example
To find f of g of zero, read g of zero equals two. Then read f of two equals three. The answer is three.
Reverse the order
For g of f of one, first find f of one equals one. Then g of one equals three. Always read the innermost function first.
When undefined
For g of f of negative two, f gives negative five. The g graph does not accept negative five, so the composition is undefined.
Graph B
The parabola p of x equals x squared minus four, and the line q of x equals one minus x. Read the inner graph, then the outer graph.
Nonlinear example
For p of q of two, q of two equals negative one. Then p of negative one equals negative three.
Solve backward
If f of g of x equals seven, find where f equals seven. Its input must be four. Now solve g of x equals four, giving x equals two.
Domain of a composition
For f of g of x, g accepts x from negative three to three. Also g of x must lie from negative three to four. The combined domain is negative three through two.
Exam checklist
Inner first. Check the input domain. Move to the outer graph. Check the output is a valid outer input. Read the final value.
Practice next
Try all eighteen practice problems, check your worked solutions, and complete the five-question lesson test.
video_ar: مقدمة
النهارده هنتعلم تركيب الدوال من الرسوم البيانية، وإزاي نراجع مجال كل دالة.
الفكرة الأساسية
التعبير إف لجي لإكس معناه نحسب جي الأول، وبعدها نستخدم الناتج كمدخل للدالة إف.
الرسم الأول
عندنا إف لإكس تساوي اتنين إكس ناقص واحد، وجي لإكس تساوي إكس زائد اتنين، وكل رسم له حدود واضحة.
مثال أول
لحساب إف لجي لصفر، جي لصفر تساوي اتنين، وبعدها إف لاتنين تساوي تلاتة.
عكس الترتيب
لو عكسنا الترتيب لازم نبدأ بالدالة اللي جوه الأقواس. غالبا النتيجة بتتغير.
القيمة غير المعرفة
إف لسالب اتنين تساوي سالب خمسة، لكن جي مش معرفة عند سالب خمسة، يبقى التركيب غير معرف.
رسم تاني
الدالة بي هي إكس تربيع ناقص أربعة، والدالة كيو هي واحد ناقص إكس.
مثال غير خطي
كيو لاتنين تساوي سالب واحد، وبي لسالب واحد تساوي سالب تلاتة.
الحل بالعكس
لو إف لجي لإكس تساوي سبعة، بندور على المدخل اللي إف عنده تساوي سبعة، وبعدها نرجع لجي.
مجال التركيب
لازم إكس يكون في مجال جي، وكمان جي لإكس تكون في مجال إف. التقاطع هو المجال الصحيح.
نصيحة الامتحان
ابدأ من الداخل، راجع المجال، انتقل للدالة الخارجية، واقرأ الناتج النهائي.
الخطوة الجاية
حل تمنتاشر سؤال تدريب، وراجع الحلول، وبعدها اختبر نفسك في خمس أسئلة.
